They concluded that there was no compelling evidence that heterozygous PARK2 mutations, alone or combined with known risk factors (SNCA, MAPT, APOE, smoking, coffee intake), are associated with PD.
quotes: In whites, having 1 CNV was not associated with increased risk (odds ratio 1.05, p = 0.89) or earlier onset of PD (64.7 ± 8.6 heterozygous vs 58.5 ± 11.8 normal).
There is no compelling evidence for association of heterozygous PARK2 mutations, by themselves or in combination with known risk factors, with PD.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with Parkinson disease onset at or before age 50 years from 13 movement disorders centers and found PRKN mutations in 6.7%: 33 heterozygotes and 27 homozygotes or compound heterozygotes. Hispanic patients were more likely to carry PRKN mutations than non-Hispanic patients (15.6% vs 5.9%).
quotes: One hundred fifty-eight (16.6%) participants had mutations, including 64 (6.7%) PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) GBA, and 1 (0.2%) DJ1.
Hispanic individuals were more likely to be PRKN carriers than non-Hispanic individuals (15.6% vs 5.9%, P = .003).

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that age at onset was significantly younger in PRKN mutation carriers than in carriers of other mutations. Biallelic PRKN mutations were found in 35% of patients with onset at or before age 20 years, compared with 0.5% of those with onset at 41 to 50 years.
quotes: AAO was significantly younger among PRKN mutation carriers than among carriers of all other mutations (p <0.001).
Carriers of 2 PRKN mutations | 35% (6) | 17% (8) | 3% (10 | 0.5% (3)

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) noted that PRKN carriers were more likely than LRRK2 carriers to report a family history of PD, even though PRKN disease is considered recessive. They suggested that the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the idea that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk factor for early-onset PD.
quotes: PRKN carriers were more likely to report a FHPD than LRRK2 carriers, despite the fact that LRRK2 is autosomal dominant and PRKN is considered a recessive disorder.
Also, the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the notion that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk of EOPD.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) concluded that patients with early-onset PD who are of Jewish or Hispanic ancestry, who had onset at or before age 30 years, or who have a first-degree relative with PD may benefit from genetic counseling. Because penetrance is unknown, they saw little or no role for predictive or prenatal testing.
quotes: In summary, EOPD individuals of Jewish or Hispanic ancestry, those with AAO ≤ 30, and those with a family history of PD in a first-degree relative may benefit from genetic counseling.
Therefore, there is little or no role for genetic testing for PD in family planning, predictive, or prenatal testing at this time.

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) screened 956 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset before 51 years) from 13 centers and found parkin mutations in 64 (6.7%): 3.9% heterozygous, 0.6% homozygous, and 2.2% compound heterozygous. Mutation prevalence declined with age at onset, from 57% with onset before 20 years to 3% with onset at 40 to 50 years.
quotes: Sixty-four PD cases (6.7%) had parkin mutations (3.9% heterozygous, 0.6% homozygotes, 2.2% compound heterozgyotes).

The prevalence of mutations declined with AAO from 57% (8/14) in cases with AAO <20, 30% (13/43) in cases with AAO 20–29, 9% (23/254) in cases with AAO 30–39 and 3% (20/644) in those with AAO 40–50 (test for linear trend p<0.001).

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found copy number variation in 52.3% of parkin mutation carriers: 31.6% of heterozygotes, 83.3% of homozygotes, and 81.0% of compound heterozygotes.
quotes: CNV was present in 52.3% of carriers (31.6% heterozygotes, 83.3% homozygotes, 81.0% compound heterozygotes).

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that Hispanic ethnicity was associated with carrying a parkin mutation (OR 2.7 vs white non-Hispanics). The exon 3-4 deletion and 255delA were common among Hispanics, especially Puerto Ricans. The 255delA mutation was not found in 139 Caribbean Hispanic controls.
quotes: Six cases (5 Puerto Rican and one Mexican carried deletions of exon 3–4. Both exon 3–4 homozygotes were of Puerto Rican descent.
The second most common mutation in Hispanics was 255delA, present in three Puerto Ricans in association with the exon 3–4 deletion and one Mexican heterozygote.
We did not detect this mutation in 139 controls of Caribbean Hispanic descent.

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that compound heterozygotes and homozygotes each had a significantly younger age at onset than heterozygotes, and every carrier group had a younger onset than noncarriers. Younger onset (before 40 years) and a family history of PD in a first-degree relative were associated with carrying any parkin mutation.
quotes: Each mutation carrier group had significantly younger AAO than the non-carrier group Compound heterozygotes and homozygotes each had a significantly younger AAO than heterozygotes.

Younger age at onset (<40 years) (odds ratio [OR], 5.0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-8.8; P = .001), Hispanic race/ethnicity (OR compared with white non-Hispanic race/ethnicity, 2.7; 95% CI, 1.3-5.7; P = .009), and family history of PD in a first-degree relative

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that dystonia as a presenting sign did not differ between parkin carriers (0%) and noncarriers (1.7%). Response to levodopa also did not differ (93.4% of carriers vs 90.5% of noncarriers).
quotes: Dystonia, as a presenting sign did not differ between carriers (0%) and non-carriers (1.7%) of parkin mutations (p=0.4) Similarly there was no difference in reported response to levodopa; 93.4% of carriers compared to 90.5% of non-carriers reported a response to anti-parkinson medications

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2010) found that heterozygous parkin carriers had a younger age at onset than noncarriers after adjustment for ethnicity and family history. They suggested that parkin heterozygosity may increase susceptibility to PD rather than directly cause it.
quotes: supports the concept that parkin heterozygosity is a susceptibility factor for PD.
These findings suggest that parkin heterozgyosity may increase PD susceptibility rather than directly causing PD.

notes.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) found that fibroblasts from 5 patients with homozygous or compound heterozygous parkin mutations had lower mitochondrial membrane potential (by 30% in glucose and 70% in galactose medium), complex I activity lower by about 42%, reduced complex I-linked ATP production, and cellular ATP levels reduced by 58%; complex II, III, and IV activities were not reduced.
quotes: Mitochondrial membrane potential was lower in all 5 parkin mutant fibroblast cultures by an average of 30% (Fig. 1A; p < 0.01).
complex I activity was lower by an average of 42% in parkin mutant fibroblasts compared to controls
The lower complex I-linked ATP production also results in an overall decrease of cellular ATP levels by 58% in the parkin mutant fibroblasts

notes.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) found increased mitochondrial branching in parkin-mutant fibroblasts, which correlated with lower complex I-linked ATP production and complex I activity, and FRAP assays showed reduced functional connectivity of the mitochondrial matrix that worsened after rotenone exposure.
quotes: The lower complex I linked ATP production correlates with an increase in both the degree of mitochondrial branching (form factor, R2 = 0.903, p < 0.001; Fig 3E)
Overall, these results show that parkin deficient fibroblasts have a basal defect in functional connectivity that is enhanced by rotenone.

notes.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) showed that siRNA knockdown of parkin by 80% in control fibroblasts reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP levels and increased mitochondrial branching, whereas 50% knockdown, mimicking haploinsufficiency, had no effect; the authors concluded this was consistent with true recessive inheritance and did not support heterozygosity as a PD risk factor.
quotes: Parkin protein levels were reduced by 80% in siRNA treated control fibroblasts compared to mock transfected controls at 5 days post transfection
In contrast, 50% knockdown of parkin, mimicking haploinsufficiency in human patient tissue, did not result in impaired mitochondrial transmembrane potential or alteration of mitochondrial morphology
This is consistent with true recessive inheritance and would not support the concept that heterozygosity for parkin is a risk factor for PD.

notes.statement: Mortiboys et al. (2008) found that treatment of parkin-mutant fibroblasts with the glutathione precursor OTCA restored mitochondrial membrane potential to 95% of control levels and fully restored cellular ATP, apparently through a compensatory increase in complex II activity rather than correction of the complex I defect; glutathione methyl ester gave only partial rescue.
quotes: Treatment of all 5 parkin mutant fibroblasts with 10μM OTCA showed improvements of mitochondrial membrane potential in every individual patient, with the average membrane potential being restored to 95% of control levels
This suggests that the observed rescue effect of mitochondrial membrane potential is due to a compensatory increase in complex II activity rather than a rescue of the complex I defect.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2008) screened the Parkin gene for point mutations and exon deletions/duplications in 247 probands with Parkinson disease with onset at 50 years or younger. They found mutations in 25 probands (10.1%), and 18 of these (72.0%) were heterozygotes.
quotes: Parkin mutations were identified in 25 probands with PD (10.1%), 18 (72.0%) of whom were heterozygotes.

notes.statement: Using the kin-cohort method, Wang et al. (2008) estimated the cumulative incidence of PD to age 65 years in Parkin carrier relatives at 7.0% (95% CI, 0.4%-71.9%). This compared with 1.7% in noncarrier relatives of cases (P = .59) and 1.1% in relatives of controls. The authors concluded that age-specific penetrance among Parkin carriers, in particular heterozygotes, deserves further study.
quotes: The cumulative incidence of PD to age 65 years in carrier relatives (age-specific penetrance) was estimated to be 7.0% (95% confidence interval, 0.4%-71.9%), compared with 1.7% (95% confidence interval, 0.8%-3.4%) in noncarrier relatives of the cases (P = .59)
Age-specific penetrance among Parkin carriers, in particular heterozygotes, deserves further study.

notes.statement: Kay et al. (2007) sequenced the parkin gene in 302 patients with Parkinson disease and 301 control subjects and replicated the findings in 1,260 more patients and 1,657 more controls. They found 34 variants, 21 of them novel: 12 polymorphisms and 22 rare variants. Patients and controls did not differ in the frequency, type, or functional location of the variants.
quotes: A total of 302 patients and 301 control subjects were sequenced, and findings were replicated in 1,260 additional patients and 1,657 control subjects.

Thirty-four variants were detected, of which 21 were novel; 12 were polymorphisms and 22 were rare variants. Patients and control subjects did not differ in the frequency, type, or functional location of the variants.

notes.statement: Kay et al. (2007) found that P437L, a common parkin mutation thought to be pathogenic, was present in unaffected control subjects. They concluded that a single heterozygous point mutation in a patient, without a second mutation, should not be taken as the cause of disease unless family data and functional studies support it.
quotes: Even P437L, a common mutation thought to be pathogenic, was present in unaffected control subjects.
The mere presence of a single point mutation in a patient, in the absence of a second mutation, should not be taken as a cause of disease unless corroborated by family data and functional studies.

notes.statement: Kay et al. (2007) concluded that their study did not support the idea that heterozygous parkin sequence variants (mutations or polymorphisms) are risk factors for Parkinson disease. Whether heterozygous dosage anomalies are associated with PD remained to be determined.
quotes: This study does not support the notion that heterozygous parkin sequence variants (mutations or polymorphisms) are risk factors for PD. Whether heterozygous dosage anomalies are associated with PD remains to be determined.

notes.statement: Chien et al. (2006) found by cDNA analysis that the IVS1+1G-T splice-site parkin mutation resulted in total loss of parkin transcript in homozygous carriers, delineating it as a loss-of-function mutation.
quotes: cDNA analysis confirmed the total loss of parkin transcript in homozygous mutation carriers, delineating this as a loss-of-function mutation.

notes.statement: In a genetic isolate from north-eastern Brazil in which genealogical studies connected 255 individuals, 15 with PD, Chien et al. (2006) found homozygosity in PD patients for markers across the PARK2 locus.
quotes: Genealogical studies could connect 255 individuals, of whom 15 had PD.
Haplotype analysis revealed homozygosity in the PD patients for markers across the PARK2 locus.

notes.statement: Chien et al. (2006) noted the absence of PD in heterozygous carriers of the parkin mutation, indicating a genuinely recessive nature and suggesting that parkin haploinsufficiency is not a relevant risk factor for early- or late-onset PD, although it could facilitate the emergence of neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism; one heterozygous carrier had likely neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism.
quotes: The case with neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism and 13 of 15 healthy relatives were heterozygous carriers of the mutation.

The absence of PD in heterozygous carriers indicates a genuinely recessive nature of this mutation, suggesting that parkin haploinsufficiency is not a relevant risk factor for early- or late-onset PD. However, parkin haploinsufficiency could facilitate the emergence of neuroleptic-induced parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Pramstaller et al. (2005) described a 7-generation pedigree of 196 individuals, 25 of whom had levodopa-responsive parkinsonism, with Parkin mutations found in 77 subjects. Of the 25 patients, 5 were compound heterozygotes, 8 carried a single heterozygous mutation, 7 had no Parkin mutation, and the status of 5 deceased patients was unknown.
quotes: We report the clinical, genetic, and neuropathological findings of a seven generation-spanning pedigree with 196 individuals, 25 of whom had levodopa-responsive parkinsonism. Genetic analyses indicated Parkin mutations in 77 subjects.
The mutational status of five deceased patients was unknown, and seven PD patients had no Parkin mutation.

notes.statement: Pramstaller et al. (2005) found by survival analysis that the age-at-onset distribution differed significantly between patients with compound heterozygous Parkin mutations and both heterozygous carriers and patients without detectable Parkin mutations.
quotes: Survival analyses showed a significant difference in the age-at-onset distribution between patients with compound heterozygous mutations and the groups of heterozygous carriers and subjects without detectable Parkin mutations.

notes.statement: In a 73-year-old compound heterozygous patient, Pramstaller et al. (2005) found that surviving neurons were immunoreactive with antibodies to the Parkin N terminus but not to the IBR domain, which had been deleted by both mutations. The patient's brain also showed alpha-synuclein-positive Lewy bodies.
quotes: Surviving neurons were reactive with antibodies to the N terminus of Parkin but not the In-Between-RING ("IBR") domain, which had been deleted by both mutations.

notes.statement: Ohsawa et al. (2005) performed nerve conduction studies in 9 PARK2 patients and 8 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease and found significantly reduced sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude in 8 of the PARK2 patients, most of whom were asymptomatic. They suggested that sensory axonal neuropathy may be a common clinical feature of PARK2.
quotes: found a significant reduction of sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude in eight PARK2 patients who mostly remained asymptomatic
These data suggest that sensory axonal neuropathy may be a common clinical feature of PARK2

notes.statement: Ohsawa et al. (2005) proposed that reduced sural SNAP amplitude could serve as a diagnostic indicator of PARK2.
quotes: a reduced amplitude of sural SNAP could be a diagnostic indicator of PARK2

notes.statement: Khan et al. (2005) used 18F-dopa PET to study 13 unrelated asymptomatic carriers of a single parkin mutation and found significantly reduced 18F-dopa uptake in the caudate, putamen, and ventral and dorsal midbrain compared with control subjects. Four of the 13 carriers had subtle extrapyramidal signs.
quotes: The authors used 18F-dopa PET to study 13 asymptomatic parkin heterozygotes and found a significant reduction of (18)F-dopa uptake in caudate, putamen, ventral, and dorsal midbrain compared with control subjects. Four had subtle extrapyramidal signs.

notes.statement: Khan et al. (2005) concluded that although parkin disease is usually autosomal recessive, parkin heterozygosity is a risk factor for nigrostriatal dysfunction and may contribute to late-onset Parkinson disease in some carriers.
quotes: Parkin disease is usually autosomal recessive
Parkin heterozygosity is a risk factor for nigrostriatal dysfunction and in some may contribute to late-onset Parkinson disease.

notes.statement: Sasaki et al. (2004) concluded that a variety of parkin gene abnormalities may produce pathologic differences in the degree and distribution of neuronal degeneration, including the absence or presence of Lewy bodies, and that a relationship between parkin-induced parkinsonism and idiopathic Parkinson disease may exist.
quotes: A variety of parkin gene abnormalities may produce pathologic differences in the degree and distribution of neuronal degeneration, including the absence or presence of Lewy bodies. A relationship between parkin-induced parkinsonism and idiopathic Parkinson disease (PD) may exist.

notes.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) screened all 12 parkin exons by sequencing and dosage analysis in 39 movement-disorder clinic patients with PD onset at or before age 40 years. They found mutations in 7 patients (18%), 2 of them compound heterozygous. Ten percent of the clinic's PD patients had early onset, and the mutation frequency was 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.19).
quotes: Mutations were found in 7/39 patients.
In conclusion, parkin mutations are common in the clinic setting: 10% of PD patients had early-onset and 18% of them had parkin mutations.
Mutation frequency was 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.19).

notes.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) found that 78% of parkin mutations in early-onset PD patients were deletions or multiplications. None of the point mutations found in patients was present in 96 controls, although a novel R402W substitution was found in 1 patient and 1 control.
quotes: Seventy-eight percent of mutations were deletions/multiplications.
None of the point mutations found in patients were detected in 96 controls.

notes.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) noted that 70% of parkin cases were heterozygous and that it was unclear whether heterozygous mutations are pathogenic. If parkin is recessive, only 5% of early-onset cases, those with compound mutations, could be attributed to this locus.
quotes: However, if parkin is recessive, only 5% of early-onset cases who had compound mutations could be attributed to this locus.
Seventy percent of parkin cases were heterozygous. It is unclear whether heterozygous mutations are pathogenic.

notes.statement: Poorkaj et al. (2004) concluded that parkin cases can present as typical idiopathic PD that can be distinguished only by molecular testing. They added that parkin-based diagnosis and counseling require a better understanding of the mode of inheritance, penetrance, and carrier frequencies.
quotes: parkin cases can present as typical idiopathic PD, distinguishable only by molecular testing.
parkin-based diagnosis and counseling require a better understanding of the mode of inheritance, penetrance, and carrier frequencies.

notes.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) compared 146 early-onset parkinsonism patients with parkin mutations to 250 without and found that no single sign distinguished the groups. On multivariate analysis, dystonia at onset and brisk reflexes correlated with age at onset rather than with the presence of parkin mutation; the younger the age at onset, the slower the evolution of disease.
quotes: Although no single sign distinguished the groups
dystonia at onset and brisk reflexes were not longer significantly different but were correlated with age at onset rather than the presence of the parkin mutation
the younger the age at onset the slower the evolution

notes.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) found that carriers of at least one missense parkin mutation had a higher UPDRS motor score than those carrying two truncating mutations, and that missense mutations in functional domains of parkin resulted in earlier onset.
quotes: carriers of at least one missense mutation had a higher United Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale motor score than those carrying two truncating mutations
missense mutations in functional domains of parkin resulted in earlier onset

notes.statement: Lohmann et al. (2003) found that patients with a single heterozygous parkin mutation had significantly later and more asymmetrical onset and more frequent levodopa-induced fluctuations and dystonia than patients with two mutations.
quotes: Patients with a single heterozygous mutation had significantly later and more asymmetrical onset and more frequent levodopa-induced fluctuations and dystonia than patients with two mutations.

notes.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) had previously found linkage of idiopathic PD to the chromosome 6 region containing the Parkin gene (D6S305, lod score 5.47). The linkage was in families with at least one member whose age at onset was younger than 40 years.
quotes: Previously, we detected linkage of idiopathic PD to the region on chromosome 6 containing the Parkin gene (D6S305, logarithm of odds score, 5.47) in families with at least one subject with age at onset (AAO) younger than 40 years.

notes.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) screened 174 multiplex PD families and 133 additional PD families for Parkin mutations. They found mutations in 18% of early-onset and 2% of late-onset families (5% overall). Excluding exon 7 mutations, the mean age at onset of mutation carriers was 31.5 years.
quotes: identified mutations in 18% of early-onset and 2% of late-onset families (5% of total families screened)
Excluding exon 7 mutations, the mean AAO of patients with Parkin mutations was 31.5 years.

notes.statement: Oliveira et al. (2003) found that mutations in exon 7, which encodes the first RING finger, occurred mainly in heterozygous PD patients with a later mean age at onset (49.2 years). These mutations were absent from controls (920 chromosomes). The authors suggested that heterozygous Parkin mutations, especially those in exon 7, act as susceptibility alleles for late-onset PD.
quotes: mutations in exon 7, the first RING finger (Cys253Trp, Arg256Cys, Arg275Trp, and Asp280Asn) were observed primarily in heterozygous PD patients with a much later AAO (mean AAO, 49.2 years) but were not found in controls in this study or several previous reports (920 chromosomes).
heterozygous mutations, especially those lying in exon 7, act as susceptibility alleles for late-onset form of Parkinson disease

notes.statement: Foroud et al. (2003) screened the parkin gene, using quantitative PCR and exon sequencing, in families with at least 2 sibs with PD who had early-onset PD or a positive lod score at an intron 7 marker. They identified 25 different mutations in 103 individuals from 47 families. Of these individuals, 41 had mutations in both alleles and 62 had a single mutation.
quotes: Screening of the parkin gene, by both quantitative PCR and exon sequencing, was performed in those families with either early onset PD (age onset < or =50 years) or positive lod score with a marker in intron 7 of the parkin gene.
A total of 25 different mutations in the parkin gene were identified in 103 individuals from 47 families.

notes.statement: Foroud et al. (2003) found that 35 (34%) of the subjects with parkin mutations had onset at age 60 years or older, and 30 of these 35 (86%) had a detectable mutation on only 1 allele. Few significant clinical differences were seen among individuals with 2, 1, or no mutated parkin copies, and the clinical findings of parkin-positive individuals were remarkably similar to those of patients without mutations.
quotes: Thirty-five of the subjects (34%) with a parkin mutation had an age at onset of 60 years or above with 30 of these 35 (86%) having a detectable mutation on only one parkin allele.
Few significant clinical differences were observed among the individuals with two, one, or no mutated copies of the parkin gene.
the clinical findings of parkin-positive individuals are remarkably similar to those without mutations.

notes.statement: Hoenicka et al. (2002) studied 19 Spanish kindreds with familial Parkinson disease (13 recessive, 4 dominant, 2 uncertain). They found no Park1 or Park5 mutations, but found Park2 mutations in 5 of the 13 recessive families. They concluded that Park2 mutations accounted for 38% of families with recessive parkinsonism in Spain.
quotes: To analyze the clinical and molecular data of 19 Spanish kindreds (13 with recessive, 4 with dominant, and 2 with uncertain inheritance) who have familial Parkinson disease.
None of these families have either Park1 or Park5 mutations.
Mutations in Park2 gene account for 38% of the families with recessive parkinsonism in Spain.

notes.statement: Hoenicka et al. (2002) found that heterozygous carriers of a single Park2 mutation either had no symptoms or developed symptoms in late adulthood or after brief exposure to haloperidol. They suggested that heterozygous mutations could be a risk factor for parkinsonism.
quotes: Heterozygous carriers of a single Park2 mutation either were asymptomatic or developed clinical symptoms in late adulthood or after brief exposure to haloperidol therapy.
heterozygous mutations could be a risk factor for parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) found Lewy body pathology typical of idiopathic Parkinson disease at autopsy in a compound heterozygous parkin mutation carrier, and suggested that compound heterozygous parkin mutations and loss of parkin protein may lead to early-onset parkinsonism with Lewy body pathology, while a hemizygous mutation may confer increased susceptibility to typical Parkinson disease.
quotes: These data suggest that compound heterozygous parkin mutations and loss of parkin protein may lead to early-onset parkinsonism with Lewy body pathology, while a hemizygous mutation may confer increased susceptibility to typical Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Farrer et al. (2001) sequenced the parkin gene in 38 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset before age 41 years) and followed up the families of 2 probands with mutations.
quotes: We have sequenced the parkin gene of 38 patients with early-onset Parkinson's disease (<41 years). Two probands with mutations were followed up.

notes.statement: Lücking et al. (2001) reported an Italian family with pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkinsonism due to parkin gene mutations, in which an affected father homozygous for an exon 2 triplication and an unaffected mother heterozygous for exon 3-4 deletions had a compound heterozygous affected son. They concluded that pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkin mutations has to be considered in early-onset parkinsonism.
quotes: The authors report an Italian family with pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkinsonism attributable to parkin gene mutations.
Thus, pseudo-dominant inheritance of parkin gene mutations has to be considered in early-onset parkinsonism

notes.statement: Lücking et al. (2001) recommended that sensitive screening techniques, such as semiquantitative multiplex PCR, be applied to detect parkin gene rearrangements such as exon multiplications and deletions.
quotes: sensitive screening techniques, such as semiquantitative multiplex PCR, should be applied.

notes.statement: Hedrich et al. (2001) screened 21 patients with early-onset parkinsonism. Conventional screening found 3 parkin mutations (a single-base substitution in exon 3 and small deletions in exon 9). Quantitative duplex PCR found gene dosage changes in 7 patients: heterozygous, compound heterozygous and homozygous exon deletions, plus heterozygous exon 4 duplications. Two patients carried more than 2 parkin mutations.
quotes: while alterations of gene dosage were found in seven patients
Remarkably, two patients carried more than two parkin mutations.

notes.statement: Hedrich et al. (2001) developed a quantitative duplex PCR method that uses fluorescence resonance energy transfer on the LightCycler to screen all 12 parkin exons for deletions and duplications. They concluded that mutational analysis of the parkin gene should include gene dosage studies.
quotes: To test for gene dosage alterations, we developed a new method of quantitative duplex PCR using the fluorescence resonance energy transfer technique on the LightCycler (Roche Diagnostics).

This is the first study systematically screening all 12 exons of parkin by real-time, kinetic quantification and clearly shows that mutational analysis of the parkin gene should include gene dosage studies.

notes.statement: Shimura et al. (2001) identified a protein complex in normal human brain made up of parkin as the E3 ubiquitin ligase, UbcH7 as its associated E2 enzyme, and a new 22-kD glycosylated form of alpha-synuclein (alphaSp22) as its substrate. Unlike normal parkin, mutant parkin associated with autosomal recessive PD failed to bind alphaSp22.
quotes: We have now identified a protein complex in normal human brain that includes parkin as the E3 ubiquitin ligase, UbcH7 as its associated E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme, and a new 22-kilodalton glycosylated form of alpha-synuclein (alphaSp22) as its substrate.
In contrast to normal parkin, mutant parkin associated with autosomal recessive PD failed to bind alphaSp22.

notes.statement: In an in vitro ubiquitination assay, Shimura et al. (2001) found that normal parkin, but not mutant parkin, converted alphaSp22 into polyubiquitinated high molecular weight species. AlphaSp22 accumulated in a non-ubiquitinated form in parkin-deficient PD brains. The authors concluded that loss of parkin function causes pathologic accumulation of alphaSp22. They suggested that this reaction underlies the accumulation of ubiquitinated alpha-synuclein in conventional PD.
quotes: In an in vitro ubiquitination assay, alphaSp22 was modified by normal but not mutant parkin into polyubiquitinated, high molecular weight species. Accordingly, alphaSp22 accumulated in a non-ubiquitinated form in parkin-deficient PD brains.
We conclude that alphaSp22 is a substrate for parkin's ubiquitin ligase activity in normal human brain and that loss of parkin function causes pathological alphaSp22 accumulation.

notes.statement: Using PET, Portman et al. (2001) found that two brothers with early-onset parkinsonism caused by parkin mutation had cerebral energy metabolism that did not differ, but a nigrostriatal dopaminergic pattern clearly different from that of sporadic Parkinson disease. They concluded that parkinsonism in these patients was pathophysiologically different from PD.
quotes: Energy metabolism did not differ, but the nigrostriatal dopaminergic pattern was clearly different than that of sporadic PD.
Thus parkinsonism in these two patients was shown to be pathophysiologically different than PD.

notes.statement: Hayashi et al. (2000) found, at autopsy of a 70-year-old man with AR-JP and a homozygous parkin exon 4 deletion, loss of pigmented neurons and gliosis in the substantia nigra pars compacta (most pronounced medially and ventrolaterally) and locus ceruleus, low melanin content in remaining nigral neurons, and no Lewy bodies on alpha-synuclein immunostaining. They also found neuronal loss and fibrillary gliosis in the substantia nigra pars reticulata, which had not been reported previously in AR-JP.
quotes: Pathologic examination of autopsy specimens from this patient revealed loss of pigmented neurons and gliosis in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNPC), being most pronounced in the medial and ventrolateral regions, and locus ceruleus (LC).
An additional, significant finding in this patient was neuronal loss and fibrillary gliosis in the substantia nigra pars reticulata; this feature has not been reported previously in AR-JP.

notes.statement: In a large South Tyrolean pedigree with adult-onset tremor-dominant parkinsonism that appeared to be autosomal dominant, Klein et al. (2000) used haplotype analysis to exclude linkage to the autosomal dominant parkinsonism regions on chromosomes 2p, 4p, and 4q. The analysis implicated the parkin locus on chromosome 6q instead.
quotes: Haplotype analysis excluded linkage to the chromosome 2p, 4p, and 4q regions that harbor genes associated with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, but implicated the parkin locus on chromosome 6q.

notes.statement: Klein et al. (2000) concluded that the phenotypic spectrum of parkin mutations is broader than previously reported. Patients with compound heterozygous parkin deletions were clinically indistinguishable from most patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease. The authors suggested that the gene may be important in the more frequent late-onset typical Parkinson disease.
quotes: The patients were clinically indistinguishable from most patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

We conclude that the phenotypic spectrum associated with mutations in the parkin gene is broader than previously reported, suggesting that this gene may be important in the etiology of the more frequent late-onset typical Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Mori et al. (1998) found neurofibrillary tangles and argyrophilic astrocytes in the cerebral cortex and brainstem nuclei of a patient with 6q-linked AR-JP, findings not previously reported in AR-JP, and suggested pathologic heterogeneity of 6q-linked AR-JP.
quotes: The later findings, which have not been reported previously in AR-JP, suggest the pathologic heterogeneity of 6q-linked AR-JP.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (1998) found linkage of autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism to 6q25.2-q27 in 15 families from 4 distinct ethnic backgrounds; a full genomic screen excluded other candidate regions. Recombination events restricted the locus to a 6.9-cM region.
quotes: We found linkage to this region in a group of 15 families from four distinct ethnic backgrounds. A full genomic screen excluded other candidate regions.
Recombination events restricted the JP locus to a 6.9-cM region and excluded SOD2.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (1998) mapped the manganese superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2) within the detailed genetic map of the region and excluded it as the juvenile parkinsonism gene by recombination. Apparent homozygosity for null alleles at D6S955 in one family suggested a deletion and finer localization of the locus.
quotes: We have constructed a detailed genetic map of the linked region and have mapped the position of the manganese superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2).
The apparent homozygosity for null alleles at D6S955 in one family suggested a deletion and finer localization of the JP locus.

notes.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) tested 1 Algerian and 10 European multiplex families with early-onset Parkinson disease for linkage to 6q25.2-q27 using marker D6S305. Homogeneity analysis gave a conditional probability of linkage greater than 0.9 in 8 families. Haplotype reconstruction and the smallest region of homozygosity in 2 consanguineous families narrowed the candidate interval to 11.3 cM.
quotes: We have tested one Algerian and 10 European multiplex families with early-onset Parkinson disease for linkage to this locus, with marker D6S305.
Homogeneity analysis provided a conditional probability in favor of linkage of >.9 in eight families
determination of the smallest region of homozygosity in two consanguineous families reduced the candidate interval to 11.3 cM

notes.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) concluded that PARK2 appears to be an important locus for AR-JP in European patients.
quotes: PARK2 appears to be an important locus for AR-JP in European patients.

notes.statement: Tassin et al. (1998) found that the clinical spectrum of PARK2-linked disease was broader than previously reported: age at onset reached 58 years, and some patients had painful dystonia.
quotes: The clinical spectrum of the disease in our families, with age at onset <=58 years and the presence of painful dystonia in some patients, is broader than that reported previously.

notes.statement: Saito et al. (1998) carried out detailed linkage analysis of autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism using densely spaced markers on 6q25.2-27. The highest cumulative pairwise lod score was 9.13 at D6S1579 (theta = 0.05). The highest multipoint lod score was 12.4 at a locus 3 cM telomeric to D6S1599. Obligate recombination events narrowed the candidate region to 13 cM between D6S1579 and D6S264.
quotes: Pairwise linkage analysis revealed the highest cumulative maximal lod score of 9.13 at D6S1579 (theta = 0.05), and multipoint linkage analysis revealed the highest cumulative lod score of 12.4 at the locus 3 cM telomeric to D6S1599.
Observation of obligate recombination events narrowed the candidate region to a 13-cM region between D6S1579 and D6S264.

notes.statement: Saito et al. (1998) found strong linkage disequilibrium between the AR-JP locus and markers D6S1579 and D6S1599 (P < 0.0001 for both). They suggested that the AR-JP gene most likely lies near the 4-cM region spanning these two markers.
quotes: we identified two marker loci, D6S1579 and D6S1599, which exhibit strong linkage disequilibrium with the AR-JP locus
These results suggest that the candidate region for the AR-JP gene is most likely located near the 4-cM region encompassing D6S1579 and D6S1599.

notes.statement: Saito et al. (1998) described autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism as a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder with parkinsonism that responds to levodopa. Mean age at onset was 23.2 years.
quotes: Autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) (MIM 600116) is a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder characterized by levodopa-responsive parkinsonism with a mean age at onset of 23.2 years.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) studied 17 families with early-onset parkinsonism with diurnal fluctuation (EPDF). Multipoint linkage analysis gave a peak lod score of 14.2 at 1.0 cM telomeric to D6S305 and placed the locus in the 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S253, the same position as the ARJP locus. The highest two-point lod score was 10.13 at theta = 0 for D6S305.
quotes: Multipoint linkage analysis gave a peak lod score of 14.2 at 1.0 cM telomeric to D6S305 and placed the disease locus in the 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S253, which is exactly the same position mapped for autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism
The highest two-point lod score was obtained at D6S305 (10.13 at theta = 0).

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) noted that a pathologic study of one EPDF case showed selective neuronal degeneration in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra, without Lewy body formation. They suggested that the disease could be characterized by a benign clinical course.
quotes: A pathologic study of one case of EPDF showed selective neuronal degeneration in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra without Lewy body formation.
This disease could be characterized by a benign clinical course and relatively selective degeneration of nigral dopaminergic neurons with no Lewy body formation.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) suggested that EPDF has multiple founder mutations. They based this on the high rate of nonconsanguinity (8 of 17 families), the absence of commonly shared haplotypes, and the wide geographic spread of the families' origins.
quotes: A high proportion of nonconsanguinity (8/17 families), the absence of commonly shared haplotypes, and the widespread geographic distribution of the families' origins suggest that EPDF has multiple founder mutations.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1998) concluded that EPDF and ARJP are allelic disorders. They proposed that both belong to the spectrum of a single clinicogenetic entity, chromosome 6q-linked parkinsonism.
quotes: The authors concluded that EPDF and ARJP are allelic disorders and should be included in the spectrum of a single-clinicogenetic entity of chromosome 6q-linked parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) noted that AR-JP maps to 6q25.2-q27 and is strongly linked to markers D6S305 and D6S253. D6S305 was deleted in one Japanese AR-JP patient.
quotes: Autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) maps to the long arm of chromosome 6 (6q25.2-q27) and is linked strongly to the markers D6S305 and D6S253; the former is deleted in one Japanese AR-JP patient.

notes.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) used positional cloning within a microdeletion to isolate a 2,960-bp cDNA. Its 1,395-bp open reading frame encodes a 465-amino-acid protein with moderate similarity to ubiquitin at the N terminus and a RING-finger motif at the C terminus. The authors named the protein parkin.
quotes: By positional cloning within this microdeletion, we have now isolated a complementary DNA done of 2,960 base pairs with a 1,395-base-pair open reading frame, encoding a protein of 465 amino acids with moderate similarity to ubiquitin at the amino terminus and a RING-finger motif at the carboxy terminus.
we have therefore named the protein product 'Parkin'

notes.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) found that the parkin gene spans more than 500 kb and contains 12 exons.
quotes: The gene spans more than 500 kilobases and has 12 exons

notes.statement: Kitada et al. (1998) found a 4.5-kb parkin transcript that was expressed in many human tissues and was abundant in brain, including the substantia nigra. The transcript was shorter in brain tissue from one group of exon 4-deleted patients.
quotes: A 4.5-kilobase transcript that is expressed in many human tissues but is abundant in the brain, including the substantia nigra, is shorter in brain tissue from one of the groups of exon-4-deleted patients.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) used linkage analysis in 13 families with autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism (AR-JP) to map the gene to chromosome 6q25.2-27, including the SOD2 locus. Maximal cumulative pairwise lod scores were 7.26 at D6S305 (theta = 0.03) and 7.71 at D6S253 (theta = 0.02).
quotes: By extending the linkage analysis to 13 families with AR-JP, we discovered strong evidence for the localization of the AR-JP gene at chromosome 6q25.2-27, including the SOD2 locus, with the maximal cumulative pairwise LOD scores of 7.26 and 7.71 at D6S305 (theta = .03) and D6S253 (theta = .02), respectively.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) used obligate recombination events and multipoint linkage analysis to place the AR-JP gene in a 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S264.
quotes: Observation of obligate recombination events, as well as multipoint linkage analysis, placed the AR-JP gene in a 17-cM interval between D6S437 and D6S264.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) first found a family with AR-JP in which the disease segregated perfectly with a diallelic polymorphism of the Mn-superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2). This finding led them to extend the linkage analysis to more families.
quotes: By linkage analysis of diallelic polymorphism of the Mn-superoxide dismutase gene (SOD2), we found a family with AR-JP showing perfect segregation of the disease with the SOD2 locus.

notes.statement: Matsumine et al. (1997) described AR-JP as a levodopa-responsive parkinsonism. Its pathology is a highly selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra.
quotes: An autosomal recessive form of juvenile Parkinsonism (AR-JP) (MIM 600116) is a levodopa-responsive Parkinsonism whose pathological finding is a highly selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the zona compacta of the substantia nigra.

notes.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) strongly suspected autosomal recessive inheritance of juvenile parkinsonism in 12 Japanese families because the parents were consanguineous in all but one family and all patients belonged to a single generation.
quotes: Because the marriages of the parents in all but one family were consanguineous and all patients were only first generation, an autosomal-recessive trait was strongly suspected.

notes.statement: Ishikawa and Tsuji (1996) found female predominance, a mean age at onset of 27.8 years, and slow progression in AR-JP. They concluded that the similarity of clinical findings among these patients, and their differences from other types of parkinsonism, indicated that AR-JP is a distinct clinical entity.
quotes: Analysis of the clinical features showed female predominance, mean age at onset 27.8 years, and slow progression.
The similarity of clinical findings in these patients, and the differences from other types of parkinsonism, indicates that AR-JP is distinct clinical entity.

notes.statement: Takahashi et al. (1994) found at autopsy of an affected woman neuronal loss and gliosis in the medial and ventrolateral substantia nigra pars compacta, with reduced neuron numbers and low melanin content elsewhere in the SNPC and locus ceruleus but no gliosis or extraneuronal free melanin suggestive of a neurodegenerative process. There were no Lewy bodies, and the pathologic picture differed from that of Lewy body Parkinson disease.
quotes: In the remainder of the SNPC and the locus ceruleus, the population of neurons was reduced and there was low melanin content in most of the neurons but no detectable gliosis or extraneuronal free melanin pigment suggestive of a neurodegenerative process.
The entire pathologic picture was different from that of Lewy body Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Bonifati et al. (1994) reported anticipation of age at onset in familial Parkinson disease.
quotes: Anticipation of onset age in familial Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Mitsui et al. (1994) reported 2 sibs with hereditary parkinsonism with pyramidal signs and cerebellar ataxia. Anticholinergics had a dramatic beneficial effect in both, but levodopa did not. The authors proposed this as a new hereditary variant of early-onset Parkinson disease, distinct from the levodopa-sensitive forms of juvenile Parkinson disease.
quotes: Two siblings who exhibited hereditary parkinsonism with pyramidal signs and cerebellar ataxia are reported. Anticholinergics had a dramatic beneficial effect in both cases, but levodopa did not.
We propose a new hereditary variant of early onset Parkinson's disease distinct from the levodopa sensitive forms of juvenile Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Ishikawa and Miyatake (1995) reported a family with autosomal dominant hereditary juvenile dystonia-parkinsonism with sleep benefit and marked levodopa response, and considered these patients to have a specific form of hereditary dystonia-parkinsonism.
quotes: From the family history and clinical findings, these patients are considered to have a specific form of hereditary dystonia-parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Yamamura et al. (1973) described paralysis agitans (parkinsonism) of early onset with marked diurnal fluctuation of symptoms.
quotes: Paralysis agitans of early onset with marked diurnal fluctuation of symptoms.
